name: illustrator-kerned-headline
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, Font: SVG
story: A full-frame programme bumper whose display headline was hand-kerned pair by pair, so Illustrator broke the single line into four <tspan> runs each carrying its own x offset; the designer drew one headline and one strapline and expects exactly two operator fields.
idioms: Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build
root attrs version/id="Layer_1"/xmlns/xmlns:xlink/x="0px"/y="0px", viewBox + width + height on tab-indented continuation lines, xml:space="preserve" wrapped onto its own line
<style type="text/css"> as a direct child of <svg>, tab-indented .stN classes, one property each
PostScript face name for a licensed foundry font: font-family:'Gotham-Bold'
kerned line written as one <text transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 240 560)"> holding four <tspan> children, all y="0", x stepping 0 / 98.7 / 392.2 / 828.4 with one decimal
a run ending in a significant trailing space (' REPOR') kept meaningful by xml:space="preserve"
tspans written on one physical line with no whitespace between them, so no stray text nodes appear
<rect y="0" ...> with the zero x omitted
whyThisMatters: Kerning is the single most common reason an Illustrator headline arrives as several tspans, and an importer that offers one field per tspan hands the operator four boxes labelled Headline, Headline 2, Headline 3, Headline 4 for one word of copy - and typing into any of them shatters the line, because the runs' x offsets were computed for the original glyphs.
